Fact.Name: Bank Account
Fact.Description: Information for the bank account you want to deposit into

Fact.Name: Wants Direct Deposit
Fact.Description: Whether the TP wants to receive a direct deposit. Otherwise, they will receive a mailed check.

Fact.Name: User's preference to pay via ACH
Fact.Description:
Whether the TP wants to make an immediate ACH payment through direct file. Otherwise, they will be have to make their payment at a different time and/or through a different method.
SCREEN SPECIFICATION (this dictionary decides the writable and its wording; the application implements it without opening an IRC document).
QUESTION AS ASKED: "Do you want to pay the amount you owe now, by direct debit from your bank account?" Answers: "Yes, pay by direct debit" / "No, I will pay another way".
HELP TEXT: "The IRS is allowed to accept payment by any commercially acceptable means, including an electronic debit from your account (IRC 6311(a); 26 U.S.C. 6311, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section6311&num=0&edition=2024). Whichever you choose, the amount is due by the filing deadline: the law fixes payment at the time and place fixed for filing the return, without regard to any extension of time for filing (IRC 6151(a); 26 U.S.C. 6151, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section6151&num=0&edition=2024). Choosing 'No' does not delay what you owe; it only means we will not schedule the debit for you. You can pay at www.irs.gov/Payments (2025 Form 1040 line 37; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040.pdf, page 2)."
ASKED WHEN: taxCalculations:/owesBalance is true. Never asked of a refund filer or a zero-balance filer; /refundViaAch is the mirror question on the refund side and the two are never both live.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: NOT DEFAULTED and NOT REFUSED. No guard fires, because both payment-date guards carry IsComplete(/payViaAch) and resolve Complete false; but /paymentSectionComplete is INCOMPLETE (every arm that mentions this fact needs it resolved), so the filer cannot finish the payment section without answering. That is deliberate: defaulting the answer either way would either schedule a debit the filer did not authorise or silently decline one they wanted.
VALIDATION: Boolean, two labelled options, no Limit. There is nothing to range-check.
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: /xmlPaymentBankAccount (its Switch resolves to nothing unless owesBalance AND this fact are both true, so the account never travels on a return that is not paying by debit); /paymentSectionComplete arms 3, 4 and 5; and both /achPaymentDateStaleAtSigning and /achPaymentDateBeyondPaymentWindow, which no longer refuse a filer who answered a date and then answered NO here.

Fact.Name: Payment date
Fact.Description:
When the user would like their payment to be processed.
SCREEN SPECIFICATION. This is the screen the two payment-date refusals send the filer back to, so its wording is part of the remedy, not decoration.
QUESTION AS ASKED: "What date should we ask your bank to send this payment?"
HELP TEXT: "Choose a date from today through the filing deadline. The amount you owe is due by that deadline no matter when you file: the law fixes payment at the time and place fixed for filing the return, determined without regard to any extension of time for filing (IRC 6151(a); 26 U.S.C. 6151, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section6151&num=0&edition=2024), and a reference to the date fixed for payment means the last day fixed for it, without regard to any extension of time for paying (IRC 6151(c); same file, line 29). Holding a filing extension does not move this date. If you are already past the deadline, the only date we can schedule is today. The debit itself is the commercially acceptable means the IRS is authorised to receive (IRC 6311(a); 26 U.S.C. 6311, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section6311&num=0&edition=2024)."
ASKED WHEN: taxCalculations:/owesBalance is true AND /payViaAch is true. Not asked of a filer paying another way; /paymentSectionComplete's not-paying-via-ACH arm treats that filer as DONE with no date at all.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: NOT DEFAULTED and NOT REFUSED. Both window guards carry IsComplete(/achPaymentDate) and resolve Complete false while it is blank, so nothing blocks submission on emptiness alone; /paymentSectionComplete is INCOMPLETE until it is answered. Never defaulted to today or to the deadline: a scheduled debit date is an instruction, and guessing one is an answer the taxpayer did not give.
VALIDATION: type Day. Effective range MIN = signing:/today and MAX = /achPaymentDateLastAllowableDate (filers:/taxDay ordinarily; signing:/today once the filer is past it, which collapses the range to a single legal date). NOTE FOR THE IMPLEMENTER, and it is the reason this range is written here in prose: THE RANGE IS NOT DECLARED AS A Limit ON THIS WRITABLE AND CANNOT BE TODAY. Both bounds are derived facts, and dictionary/ty2025/FactDictionaryModule.rng's LimitContent admits only Int, Dollar, String and Day literals, so a bound naming a Dependency fails xmllint and the dictionary build (the engine itself supports it; the repo's schema does not). Until that is lifted, the application owns the range check at entry, and the two derived flags below own it at submission.
RE-VALIDATE AT SUBMISSION, NOT ONLY AT ENTRY. These bounds MOVE with the calendar: a date that was legal when it was entered goes stale on its own, so a return that resolved clean yesterday can be blocked today with no answer having changed. No entry-time check of any kind can close that; it is why the two derived flags exist alongside the range.
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: the MeF payment record's requested payment date (this fact carries Export mef="true" directly; see the gated-twin gap recorded on /achPaymentDateStaleAtSigning), and both /achPaymentDateStaleAtSigning (date earlier than today) and /achPaymentDateBeyondPaymentWindow (date later than the last allowable date), each of which blocks submission through its alias and sends the filer back to this screen.

Fact.Name: Payment date is scheduled in the past
Fact.Description: Whether the specified payment date is in the past. The predicate moved to /achPaymentDateStaleAtSigning, which adds the /payViaAch conjunct this guard never carried, and this fact is now an alias over it so the submission block and the fact path both stay where every reader already looks. The alias is a Dependency reuse, not a second derivation of the same quantity: read /achPaymentDateStaleAtSigning for the rule, its authority and its fixtures. It stays an All-over-Derived body deliberately, because it is a protected entry of js/test/factDictionaryTests/completenessProbe.baseline.json.

Fact.Name: The elected ACH payment date has fallen behind today
Fact.Description:
The successor to paymentMethod:/achPaymentDateInThePast, which is now an alias over this fact. True when the filer has ELECTED to pay by ACH, owes a balance, and the date they scheduled the debit for is earlier than signing:/today, so the instruction on the return can no longer be carried out and the answer has to be re-taken.
THE NARROWING THIS FACT LANDS is a defect fix, not a refinement. The guard it succeeds never checked /payViaAch, so a filer who answered a payment date and then set /payViaAch to false and chose to pay some other way was still blocked by a date that feeds nothing. The module proves the date feeds nothing in that state: /xmlPaymentBankAccount is a Switch whose only Case is All(owesBalance, /payViaAch) and resolves to nothing otherwise, and /paymentSectionComplete treats a filer who is not paying via ACH as DONE with no date required at all.
COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: IsComplete(/achPaymentDate) and IsComplete(/payViaAch) are both conjuncts, so an unanswered date or an unanswered election resolves this fact to Complete false rather than Incomplete (All returns Complete false the moment any conjunct is Complete false). Neither IsComplete gates a complete-safe fact: both wrap bare Writables whose unanswered state is exactly the "source has not answered" predicate. The election-unanswered residue is refused upstream by /paymentSectionComplete, every arm of which needs /payViaAch resolved.
TIME-DEPENDENT, which almost no other refusal in this dictionary is: it reads signing:/today, so a return that resolved clean yesterday is refused today with no answer having changed. Every fixture pinning it controls signing:/todayOverride.
WHAT IS NOT LANDED HERE, named rather than assumed. The contract also asked for the intake half: a Min bound on /achPaymentDate reading signing:/today. The ENGINE supports a derived bound (limits/Min.scala and Max.scala each build theirs with CompNode.fromDerivedConfig, whose registered factories include Dependency), but this repo does not yet accept one in the dictionary: FactDictionaryModule.rng's LimitContent admits only Int, Dollar, String and Day LITERALS, so xmllint rejects a Dependency bound outright, and scripts/limit_test.py's supported() itemises it as a skip that its RATCHET turns into a live-run failure. Neither fix is available to a dictionary author today. A Limit could not retire this fact in any case: it is evaluated when the answer is given and cannot catch a date that goes stale afterwards, which is exactly what this flag catches.
NOR IS THE MeF HALF LANDED, and it is named here because /achPaymentDate's screen specification points at this paragraph for it. /achPaymentDate carries a bare Export mef="true" with NO election gate, while the account it travels with has the gated /xmlPaymentBankAccount, a Switch whose only Case is All(taxCalculations:/owesBalance, /payViaAch) (no line number: locators in this module drift). So this narrowing stops the REFUSAL but leaves a stale date reaching the return header for a filer who withdrew the election: the payment block is emitted half-gated. The remedy is a gated /xmlAchPaymentDate twin shaped exactly like /xmlPaymentBankAccount, with Export mef="true" moving off /achPaymentDate onto the twin; it binds the MeF IRSPayment record's RequestedPaymentDate. It is QUEUED, not done: the hold that used to sit on it (the e-file/MeF clause of invariant #7) was lifted, but no MeF schema is vendored under sources/ and Export mef="true" carries no element name anywhere in this repo, so the element naming is unciteable today.

Fact.Name: Require the ach payment date be today
Fact.Description: Whether to require the ach payment date be today if they are filing after the deadline

Fact.Name: Last allowable date for ach payment
Fact.Description: The last possible date for ach payment

Fact.Name: Payment date is scheduled for after tax day or last allowable date
Fact.Description: Whether the specified payment date comes after the last tax day or last allowable date. The predicate moved to /achPaymentDateBeyondPaymentWindow, which adds the /payViaAch conjunct this guard never carried, and this fact is now an alias over it so the submission block and the fact path both stay where every reader already looks. The alias is a Dependency reuse, not a second derivation of the same quantity. It stays an All-over-Derived body deliberately, because it is a protected entry of js/test/factDictionaryTests/completenessProbe.baseline.json.

Fact.Name: The elected ACH payment date is after the last allowable date
Fact.Description:
The successor to paymentMethod:/achPaymentDateAfterDeadline, which is now an alias over this fact. True when the filer has ELECTED to pay by ACH, owes a balance, and scheduled the debit for a date after /achPaymentDateLastAllowableDate, which is filers:/taxDay ordinarily and signing:/today once the filer is already past it.
THE MIRROR OF /achPaymentDateStaleAtSigning AND A DIFFERENT BODY. One flag fences the PAST edge of the window, this one the FUTURE edge, and the future edge COLLAPSES ONTO TODAY once the deadline has passed (/achPaymentDateLastAllowableDate is a Switch on /achPaymentDateMustBeToday) so that a filer past filers:/taxDay is subject to both at once and only one date is acceptable. They land together for that reason.
THE SAME NARROWING APPLIES, for the same measured reason: this guard also never checked /payViaAch, so a filer who withdrew the ACH election was refused for a date the module itself treats as feeding nothing. See the sibling for the two witnesses in the module's own body.
A STATUTORY POINT THIS FACT MUST NOT LOSE, and the one place the pair touches real tax law rather than intake hygiene: IRC 6151(c) says the date fixed for payment is the last day fixed for it "determined without regard to any extension of time for paying the tax", and 6151(a) says the same of the filing extension. The window's late edge is therefore taxDay REGARDLESS of any extension the filer holds, and a later unit that reaches for an extended date because the filer extended is wrong on the statute. /achPaymentDateLastAllowableDate is correct today for that reason and must stay so.
COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION, exactly as the sibling: IsComplete(/achPaymentDate) and IsComplete(/payViaAch) are both conjuncts, so an unanswered date or election resolves this fact to Complete false rather than Incomplete.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: automatically CLAMPING the answer into the window. Silently moving a taxpayer's scheduled debit date is an answer they did not give, and this repo's standing instrument for an entry the filer must correct is the block plus the re-ask (formW2s:/hasW2ValidationErrors, scheduleC:/scheduleCs/proprietorUnansweredOnMfj), not a guess. WHAT IS NOT LANDED: the intake half, a Max bound on /achPaymentDate reading /achPaymentDateLastAllowableDate. The engine supports a derived bound; this repo's RNG and scripts/limit_test.py do not yet accept one. The sibling fact records the same finding.

Fact.Name: Payment Section Complete
Fact.Description: The Payment Method section is as complete as it needs to be

Fact.Name: Refund Bank account
Fact.Description: The bank account used for refunds to the taxpayer. Populates the IRS XML elements corresponding to 1040 lines 35b, 35c, and 35d.

Fact.Name: Payment Bank account
Fact.Description: The bank account used for payments from the taxpayer to the IRS. Populates the IRSPayment XML elements corresponding to 1040.

Fact.Name: Refund Disbursement Code
Fact.Description: MeF Variable: Refund Disbursement Code. Acceptable values: 0 – Balance Due/Zero Balance 1 – Reloadable Prepaid Card 2 – Bank Account 3 – Paper Check 4 – Non-reloadable Merchant Gift Card 5 - Cryptocurrency 6 - Other 1 7 - Other 2

Fact.Name: Has Ultimate Bank Account
Fact.Description: When an ultimate bank account exists, MeF requires us to add information about that bank account to the return headers. If /xmlRefundDisbursementCd is any value other than (0, 3, or 4), then /xmlHasUltimateBankAccount should be true. Otherwise, it should have no value.
